messages:
james: Hey team :wave: I need help adding an adult dependent to medical + dental. She is 30, permanently disabled and lives with me. Not my child or sibling — she’s a household dependent I support financially. Can I add her midyear? Also, my ex covers her on his employer plan too; can we split the premium on Redwood payroll?
sarah-peopleops: Hi James — thanks for the details. This sounds like a QLE due to change in household/dependent status if it's a qualifying event, otherwise midyear additions usually require qualifying life events. For adult dependents with disabilities we accept documentation. Can you confirm whether she currently has other coverage and whether this is a loss/gain of coverage scenario? :thinking:
james: She currently has coverage under my ex's employer plan but he said he'd be open to switching or splitting costs. There isn't a coverage loss yet. I anticipated a midyear add because her status changed (became fully dependent on me financially earlier this year).
sarah-peopleops: Understood. Two paths: 1) If there's a formal QLE (e.g., loss of other coverage) you can enroll within 30 days of the event. 2) If no QLE, then enrollment generally waits until open enrollment unless we can document dependency and get an exception. For adult disabled dependents we need: (a) proof of disability (SSA award letter or physician letter), (b) evidence of financial support / affidavit of dependency, and (c) proof of shared residence (utility bill or lease) — all dated within 12 months. Please upload via the benefits intake form: https://intranet.redwood/benefits/upload or email benefits@redwood.com.
lee-payroll: Quick note on splitting premiums: payroll cannot split a single employee deduction between two unrelated employers. If you and your ex each want to contribute, we can set up a voluntary reimbursement arrangement (paper-based) or one of you enrolls and the other reimburses offline. If he works for a different employer, they’d have to set his payroll to deduct for that policy. We can't set two employers to split the same Redwood premium line-item.
benefits-bot: FYI — required docs checklist: SSA or doctor letter, signed Dependent Affidavit (PDF), proof of residence. Upload deadline for exceptions: 30 days from benefits request. If QLE, 30 days from event.
james: Ok, that helps. If we go the exception route, will premiums be prorated back to the event date?
sarah-peopleops: If we approve a retroactive exception we typically prorate to the first of the month of the qualifying date, but it depends on payroll cutoff. Lee can confirm payroll cycle impact. Please note tax treatment may differ if there are retroactive premium changes.
lee-payroll: Confirming — retroactive adds are prorated based on the payroll calendar. If approval is after a payroll run, the difference may be collected in the next pay period. If premiums change mid-cycle we follow the usual proration formulas. For anything complex (split reimbursement with ex), include both parties' contact info in the ticket and we'll flag for manual review.
emily: Adding from benefits team — if James can upload the SSA award letter + signed Dependent Affidavit and a recent utility bill, we can start the review. If your ex is willing to sign a short reimbursement agreement, we can attach that to the case but it won't change payroll deductions. Also, please redact any SSNs in uploads.
james: Thanks all — I will get the SSA letter and affidavit together today and upload. One more Q: will adding her make me ineligible for any HSA contributions?
sarah-peopleops: Good question. Adding an adult dependent changes your family coverage status, which can affect HSA eligibility. After enrollment change, check HSA plan docs — typically if you move from single to family HDHP coverage, HSA contribution limits change but you remain eligible if enrolled in HSA-qualified HDHP. We'll flag the HSA team on your case to confirm limits.
james: Great. Uploading now. tagging @sarah-peopleops for receipt. :thumbsup:
sarah-peopleops: Got it — I'll watch for the upload and confirm once we have the docs. If we need anything else we'll follow up in this thread. Thanks! :white_check_mark:
